title: Algebraicity from an fppf algebraic-space atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Suppose that $U$ is an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and $q:U\to F$ is a morphism of sheaves. Assume that for every $S$-scheme $Z$ in the site and every $a\in F(Z)$, the sheaf $h_Z\times_{a,F,q}U$, where $h_Z(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(W,Z)$, is an algebraic space $P_a$ over $Z$, and $P_a\to Z$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Flatness and local finite presentation for algebraic-space morphisms mean these properties on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; surjectivity means surjectivity on field-valued point classes [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$. No representability assumption on the diagonal of $F$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $v:A\to U$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space], and put $p=qv$. For each scheme $T$ and $a\in F(T)$ write $P_a=h_T\times_FU$. The sheaf $B_a=h_T\times_Fh_A$ identifies, on sections, with $P_a\times_Uh_A$, hence is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; $B_a\to P_a$ is representable surjective etale by that node. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to B_a$. Its composite with $B_a\to P_a$ is again representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The hypothesis on $P_a\to T$ says $W\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], with target chart $T\to T$, therefore gives those two properties for $B_a\to T$. It is surjective on point classes: lift a point first to $P_a$, then along the surjective etale map to $B_a$. This proves the same scheme-test atlas hypothesis for $p:h_A\to F$.

Apply step 1 at the section of $F(A)$ defined by $p$. It gives the algebraic space $R=h_A\times_Fh_A$ and two flat locally finitely presented projections $s,t:R\to A$; swapping the factors gives the assertion for the second projection. For each $T$, its sections are exactly the pairs $(x,y)\in A(T)^2$ with $p(x)=p(y)$. Thus $j=(s,t):R\to h_{A\times_SA}$ is monic and its image is an equivalence relation. The operations are $(x,x)$, $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x)$, and $((x,y),(y,z))\mapsto(x,z)$, naturally in $T$. No diagonal property of $F$ has been used.

The morphism $j$ is chartwise locally of finite type. Indeed, for a scheme chart $C\to R$, the composite $C\to A$ is locally finitely presented by step 1. To check $C\to A\times_SA$ at $c$, choose an affine target neighbourhood $D=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $j(c)$, shrink it to a principal open lying over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}K\subset A$, and choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}L$ of $c$ mapping into it with $L$ finitely generated over $K$; such a neighbourhood exists since $C\to A$ is locally finitely presented, and further principal shrinking only adjoins one inverse. The maps factor $K\to B_b\to L$. The same finite $K$-generators generate $L$ over $B_b$, and adding the image of $b^{-1}$ makes them generators over $B$. This is precisely the affine finite-type criterion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf] to $j$ and then [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable], whose target is the scheme $A\times_SA$. Hence $R$ is a scheme. Its identity chart shows that $s,t$ are flat locally finitely presented scheme maps.

source.place: Tag 04S6, reduction from algebraic-space groupoids to scheme groupoids; Tag 0462 affine finite-type argument

proof.text: The map $p$ is locally surjective for the fppf topology. Given $a\in F(T)$, take a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to B_a$. The composite $W\to T$ is flat and locally finitely presented by step 1. It is surjective: every point class of $T$ lifts through the two surjective maps $W\to B_a\to T$, and for schemes a field-valued representative gives its ordinary scheme point. Thus $\{W\to T\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. The universal pair on $B_a$ gives $w:W\to A$ with $p(w)=a|_W$.

Let $P(T)=A(T)/R(T)$. The map $[x]\mapsto p(x)$ identifies $P$ with a subpresheaf of $F$, since equality of $p$-images is exactly the kernel relation in step 2. We show directly that $F$ is its sheafification. For any fppf sheaf $G$ and any map $P\to G$, cover $T$ by lifts $x_i$ to $A$ of a section $a\in F(T)$, using step 4. The $x_i$ have equal $p$-images on overlaps, hence their classes in $P$ agree there. Their images glue uniquely in $G(T)$. Common covering refinements show independence of lifts and naturality under pullback; uniqueness follows by restriction to the lifting cover. This supplies exactly the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $Q=A/R$ for this sheafification. The unique maps $Q\to F$ and $F\to Q$ extending the common map from $P$ are inverse by uniqueness, so $F\simeq Q$.

Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-space-relation-slicing] to the schematic equivalence relation $R\rightrightarrows A$ from steps 2--3. Obtain schemes $V,D$, an equivalence relation $D\rightrightarrows V$ with flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite projections, and an isomorphism $V/D\simeq Q$. Choose an affine open cover $\{V_\alpha\}$ of $V$, with index set bounded by the size of $V$. Write $D_\alpha=D\times_{V\times_SV}(V_\alpha\times_SV_\alpha)$ and $Q_\alpha=V_\alpha/D_\alpha$. The projection $D_\alpha\to V_\alpha$ is a base change of $D\to V$ followed by open restriction. Flatness and local finite presentation follow from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), [lem-pc-flat-compose], [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1), which makes open immersions etale, and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Local quasi-finiteness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change](2) and [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens]. The other projection is identical after interchange.

Fix $\alpha$. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-relation-etale-replacement] to the affine scheme $V_\alpha$ and relation $D_\alpha$. It gives finitely many etale maps $W_i\to V_\alpha$ covering $V_\alpha$, and isomorphisms $W_i/(D_\alpha|_{W_i})\simeq\overline W_i/\overline D_i$, where the relation on the right is etale. By [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] each right-hand quotient, hence each left-hand quotient $E_i$, is an algebraic space. By [lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens] the maps $E_i\to Q_\alpha$ are representable open immersions: their input maps $W_i\to V_\alpha$ are etale, hence flat and locally finitely presented [def-weil-etale-morphism], and the relation projections are surjective because they have the diagonal section.

The maps $E_i\to Q_\alpha$ are jointly surjective as sheaves. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] says a section of $Q_\alpha$ is fppf-locally a class of a map to $V_\alpha$. Pull back the covering $\{W_i\to V_\alpha\}$ along that map; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] gives an etale covering, which is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site] and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. On its members the class lifts to the corresponding $E_i$. The finite coproduct of the $E_i$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct]; its required atlas coproduct is a finite scheme coproduct in the chosen site bound [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family, def-weil-size-convention]. Identify each $E_i$ with its image open subfunctor. Then [lem-trf-algebraic-space-open-gluing] shows $Q_\alpha$ is an algebraic space.

By [lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens], the maps $Q_\alpha\to V/D$ are representable open immersions, since $V_\alpha\to V$ are open immersions, etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1), hence flat and locally finitely presented [def-weil-etale-morphism]. They cover as sheaves: a section of $V/D$ is fppf-locally represented in $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], and the inverse images of the $V_\alpha$ form an open covering of that test scheme. On each member the representative lies in $V_\alpha$. The coproduct $\coprod_\alpha Q_\alpha$ is algebraic by [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct]. Its size condition is satisfied: take the affine cover with index bounded by $|V|$, the scheme atlases obtained in steps 7--8 (finitely many per affine piece), and their scheme coproduct in the fixed containing universe [def-weil-size-convention, lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-space-open-gluing] to obtain algebraicity of $V/D$, and transport it along $V/D\simeq Q\simeq F$. Transporting an atlas and its scheme tests along this natural isomorphism preserves exactly the defining clauses of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Empty schemes and empty covering families are included: the empty quotient is the empty algebraic space.

lean.statement: theorem fppf_space_atlas_bootstrap {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (U : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : U.obj ⟶ F) (hatlas : ∀ (T : Over S) (a : F.obj.obj (op T)), ∃ (P : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : P.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (r : P.obj.obj ⟶ U.obj.obj), IsPullback r p q.hom (yonedaEquiv.symm a) ∧ (∀ (V : Over S) (c : yoneda.obj V ⟶ P.obj.obj), IsEtale c → Flat (yoneda.preimage (c ≫ p)).left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (yoneda.preimage (c ≫ p)).left) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ p)) : IsAlgebraicSpace F
